text:
I spent the weekend testing local vector embeddings directly on Android instead of hitting our cloud API for search.

The setup was simple: I embedded a quantized 40MB transformer model on-device to handle semantic search across 10,000 offline cached items.

The results surprised me.

Network search latency went from ~220ms down to 14ms on a mid-range phone. Battery drain was negligible because the inference runs in tight bursts, and the app gained full offline search capabilities overnight.

The trade-off? Semantic retrieval accuracy dropped by about 3% compared to full-scale cloud models. But for mobile search filters and local tagging, users didn't notice any quality difference at all.

Moving heavy context processing to the client side isn't just about reducing server costs. It completely changes how responsive a mobile UI feels when users don't have to wait on a network roundtrip.

Have you tried pushing vector operations or embeddings onto the device yet, or are you still relying on cloud endpoints?
